stages.description: Load tiny dimension tables into memory arrays. Nation (25 rows) and region (5 rows) are used by many queries for nation/region filtering. All columnar files for orders, customer, supplier, part are mmap'd here so subsequent index lookups are ready.

operations.notes: 25 rows → direct array lookup by n_nationkey. No hash needed.
5 rows → direct array lookup by r_regionkey.
mmap all orders columns so orders_pk_idx lookups during lineitem scan hit page cache. 15M rows × ~50 bytes = ~750MB.
mmap customer columns for dense_pk lookups. 1.5M rows × ~80 bytes = ~120MB.
mmap supplier columns for dense_pk lookups. 100K rows × ~80 bytes = ~8MB.
mmap part columns for dense_pk lookups and part scan. 2M rows × ~50 bytes = ~100MB.

stages.description: Single-pass scan of part (2M rows). Builds per-query bitsets of qualifying p_partkey values. These bitsets are consumed during later lineitem and partsupp scans for early filtering, avoiding repeated per-row part lookups.

consumer_branches.action: set bit in part_bitset_q2[p_partkey]; store (p_partkey, p_mfgr) for final output
set bit in part_bitset_q9[p_partkey]

consumer_branches.filter: p_brand <> 'Brand#45' AND p_type NOT LIKE 'MEDIUM POLISHED%' AND p_size IN (49,14,23,45,19,3,36,9)
consumer_branches.action: set bit in part_bitset_q16[p_partkey]; store (p_partkey → p_brand, p_type, p_size) in part_attrs_q16 map
set bit in part_bitset_q20[p_partkey]

stages.notes: Parallelize with OpenMP across row chunks; each thread maintains a thread-local bitset; merge (OR) after the loop. Part is small enough (~100MB columnar) to scan in <1s even on HDD.

stages.description: Single-pass scan of lineitem (~60M rows, ~4.8GB columnar). The dominant I/O cost of the entire batch. Inside the loop, each row is simultaneously fed to all 16 consuming queries. Queries needing orders/customer/supplier/part data use O(1) dense_pk index lookups into mmap'd columns. Queries needing partsupp use the composite hash index.

consumer_branches.action: accumulate: group by (l_returnflag, l_linestatus) → sum(qty), sum(price), sum(disc_price), sum(charge), sum(discount), count. 4 groups, use fixed array.
consumer_branches.notes: ~98.6% selectivity. Almost all rows qualify.

consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk_idx[l_orderkey] → o_orderdate, o_custkey, o_shippriority. Filter o_orderdate < 9204. Probe customer_pk_idx[o_custkey] → c_mktsegment. Filter c_mktsegment = 'BUILDING'. Accumulate revenue = sum(l_extendedprice * (1-l_discount)) grouped by (l_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_shippriority). Maintain top-10 heap by revenue DESC.
consumer_branches.notes: ~51% shipdate selectivity × ~49% orderdate × ~21% mktsegment ≈ 5.2% of rows contribute.

consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk_idx[l_orderkey] → o_orderdate, o_custkey. Filter o_orderdate in [1994-01-01, 1995-01-01). Probe customer_pk_idx[o_custkey] → c_nationkey. Probe nation[c_nationkey] → n_regionkey. Filter region[n_regionkey] = 'ASIA'. Probe supplier_pk_idx[l_suppkey] → s_nationkey. Filter s_nationkey = c_nationkey (same nation). Accumulate revenue by n_name.
consumer_branches.notes: ~15.7% orderdate × ~20% region × same-nation filter. ~5 output groups.

consumer_branches.filter: l_shipdate >= 8766 (1994-01-01) AND l_shipdate < 9131 (1995-01-01) AND l_discount BETWEEN 0.05 AND 0.07 AND l_quantity < 24
consumer_branches.action: accumulate: sum(l_extendedprice * l_discount). Single scalar.
consumer_branches.notes: ~15.7% × 27.4% × 45.7% ≈ 1.97% selectivity. Pure filter+aggregate, no joins.

consumer_branches.action: probe supplier_pk_idx[l_suppkey] → s_nationkey → nation → n_name (supp_nation). Probe orders_pk_idx[l_orderkey] → o_custkey. Probe customer_pk_idx[o_custkey] → c_nationkey → nation → n_name (cust_nation). Filter (supp=FRANCE,cust=GERMANY) OR (supp=GERMANY,cust=FRANCE). Accumulate volume by (supp_nation, cust_nation, YEAR(l_shipdate)).
consumer_branches.notes: ~31.4% shipdate × (2/625) nation-pair ≈ 0.1%. 4 output groups.

consumer_branches.action: probe part_pk_idx[l_partkey] → p_type. Filter p_type = 'ECONOMY ANODIZED STEEL'. Probe orders_pk_idx[l_orderkey] → o_orderdate, o_custkey. Filter o_orderdate in [1995-01-01, 1997-01-01). Probe customer_pk_idx[o_custkey] → c_nationkey → nation → n_regionkey. Filter region = 'AMERICA'. Probe supplier_pk_idx[l_suppkey] → s_nationkey → nation → n_name. Accumulate CASE volume by o_year.
consumer_branches.notes: ~0.7% part type × 31.4% orderdate × 20% region ≈ 0.04%. 2 output groups.

consumer_branches.action: probe partsupp_composite_hash[(l_partkey, l_suppkey)] → ps_supplycost. Probe orders_pk_idx[l_orderkey] → o_orderdate → o_year. Probe supplier_pk_idx[l_suppkey] → s_nationkey → nation → n_name. Compute amount = l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount) - ps_supplycost*l_quantity. Accumulate by (nation, o_year).
consumer_branches.notes: ~0.7% part filter → ~420K qualifying lineitem rows. ~175 output groups (25 nations × 7 years).

consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk_idx[l_orderkey] → o_orderdate, o_custkey. Filter o_orderdate in [1993-10-01, 1994-01-01). Probe customer_pk_idx[o_custkey] → c_custkey, c_name, c_acctbal, c_phone, c_nationkey, c_address, c_comment. Probe nation[c_nationkey] → n_name. Accumulate revenue by customer. Maintain top-20 heap.
consumer_branches.notes: ~24.2% returnflag × 3.9% orderdate ≈ 0.94%. Top-20 output.

consumer_branches.filter: l_shipmode IN ('MAIL','SHIP') AND l_receiptdate >= 8766 (1994-01-01) AND l_receiptdate < 9131 (1995-01-01) AND l_commitdate < l_receiptdate AND l_shipdate < l_commitdate
consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk_idx[l_orderkey] → o_orderpriority. Accumulate CASE(high_priority, low_priority) counts by l_shipmode.
consumer_branches.notes: ~28.6% shipmode × ~15.7% receiptdate × date-ordering filters. 2 output groups.

consumer_branches.action: probe part_pk_idx[l_partkey] → p_type. Accumulate sum(CASE WHEN p_type LIKE 'PROMO%' THEN l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount)) and sum(l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount)). Single ratio output.
consumer_branches.notes: ~1.3% selectivity (1 month). Single scalar output.

consumer_branches.action: accumulate sum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) grouped by l_suppkey. Store in supplier_revenue array[100001].
consumer_branches.notes: ~3.9% selectivity. ~100K output groups (one per supplier). Find max in finalize.

consumer_branches.action: probe part_pk_idx[l_partkey] → p_brand, p_container. Filter p_brand='Brand#23' AND p_container='MED BOX'. For qualifying rows, accumulate per-partkey: sum(l_quantity), count, and store all (l_quantity, l_extendedprice) pairs for second-pass filtering in finalize.
consumer_branches.notes: ~0.1% part selectivity (brand × container). ~2000 qualifying parts, ~60K lineitem rows. Store detail for avg-based filtering in finalize.

consumer_branches.action: accumulate sum(l_quantity) grouped by l_orderkey into orderkey_qty_sum array (dense, 60M entries × 8 bytes = 480MB). Qualifying orderkeys (sum > 300) identified in finalize.
consumer_branches.notes: All 60M rows contribute. Dense array indexed by l_orderkey. ~57 qualifying orders (very selective HAVING).

consumer_branches.filter: l_shipmode IN ('AIR', 'AIR REG') AND l_shipinstruct = 'DELIVER IN PERSON'
consumer_branches.action: probe part_pk_idx[l_partkey] → p_brand, p_container, p_size. Apply 3-way OR condition: (Brand#12, SM cases, qty 1-11, size 1-5) OR (Brand#23, MED cases, qty 10-20, size 1-10) OR (Brand#34, LG cases, qty 20-30, size 1-15). Accumulate sum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)).
consumer_branches.notes: ~28.6% shipmode × 25% shipinstruct × ~0.3% combined part+qty filters. Single scalar output.

consumer_branches.filter: l_shipdate >= 8766 (1994-01-01) AND l_shipdate < 9131 (1995-01-01) AND part_bitset_q20[l_partkey] is set
consumer_branches.action: accumulate sum(l_quantity) grouped by (l_partkey, l_suppkey) into q20_qty_intermediate hash map. Used during partsupp scan to check ps_availqty > 0.5 * sum.
consumer_branches.notes: ~15.7% shipdate × ~0.7% part filter ≈ 0.11%. ~8.4K intermediate entries.

consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk_idx[l_orderkey] → o_orderstatus. Filter o_orderstatus = 'F'. Probe supplier_pk_idx[l_suppkey] → s_nationkey. Filter nation = 'SAUDI ARABIA'. For qualifying rows, record per-orderkey: (suppkey, l_receiptdate > l_commitdate flag). Build per-orderkey multi-supplier tracking structure for EXISTS(other supplier) AND NOT EXISTS(other late supplier) logic.
consumer_branches.notes: ~33% orderstatus=F × ~4% nation filter. Complex EXISTS/NOT EXISTS resolved per-orderkey in finalize.

stages.notes: Parallelize with OpenMP across row chunks (block_size=65536 rows). Each thread maintains thread-local accumulators for all 16 consumers. Merge thread-local results after the loop. Column access is sequential within each block for cache efficiency. HDD sequential read at ~150MB/s → ~32s I/O for 4.8GB. With 64 cores, CPU processing is not the bottleneck.

stages.description: Single-pass scan of orders (~15M rows, ~750MB). Handles Q4 and Q13 which are driven by orders and not handled during the lineitem scan. Q4 needs EXISTS check against lineitem; Q13 counts orders per customer.

consumer_branches.action: probe lineitem_orderkey_idx[o_orderkey] → (start_row, count). Scan lineitem rows in range: check EXISTS(l_commitdate < l_receiptdate). If exists, increment count for o_orderpriority group.
consumer_branches.notes: ~3.9% orderdate selectivity. 5 output groups. lineitem columns l_commitdate, l_receiptdate already mmap'd.

consumer_branches.action: increment count_per_customer[o_custkey] for qualifying orders. In finalize, build histogram of c_count values (including customers with 0 orders).
consumer_branches.notes: ~99.4% selectivity on comment filter. 1.5M customer buckets → ~40 histogram groups in finalize.

stages.notes: Parallelize with OpenMP across row chunks. Each thread maintains thread-local accumulators. Q4 does random lineitem lookups via lineitem_orderkey_idx (already mmap'd). Q13 uses atomic increments on count_per_customer array (or thread-local arrays merged after). HDD sequential read at ~150MB/s → ~5s I/O for 750MB.

stages.description: Single-pass scan of partsupp (8M rows, ~320MB). Handles Q2, Q11, Q16, Q20 which are driven by partsupp joins. Uses part bitsets from fused_scan_part and lineitem intermediates from fused_scan_lineitem.

consumer_branches.action: probe supplier_pk_idx[ps_suppkey] → s_nationkey, s_name, s_acctbal, s_address, s_phone, s_comment. Probe nation[s_nationkey] → n_name, n_regionkey. Filter region[n_regionkey] = 'EUROPE'. Track minimum ps_supplycost per ps_partkey. Store all qualifying (partkey, suppkey, supplycost, supplier_info, part_info) tuples.
consumer_branches.notes: ~0.08% part filter (size=15 × type BRASS) × 20% region ≈ 640 qualifying rows. In finalize, select rows where supplycost = min per partkey, sort, limit 100.

consumer_branches.action: probe supplier_pk_idx[ps_suppkey] → s_nationkey. Filter nation = 'GERMANY'. Accumulate sum(ps_supplycost * ps_availqty) by ps_partkey. Also accumulate global total for threshold (total * 0.0001).
consumer_branches.notes: ~4% nation filter → ~320K qualifying rows. High cardinality output groups (~200K partkeys).

consumer_branches.action: probe supplier_pk_idx[ps_suppkey] → s_comment. Filter s_comment NOT LIKE '%Customer%Complaints%'. Add ps_suppkey to distinct supplier set per (p_brand, p_type, p_size) group (looked up from part_attrs_q16).
consumer_branches.notes: ~14.7% combined part filter → ~1.18M qualifying partsupp rows. COUNT(DISTINCT ps_suppkey) per group → use HyperLogLog or small hash sets.

consumer_branches.action: probe supplier_pk_idx[ps_suppkey] → s_nationkey, s_name, s_address. Filter nation = 'CANADA'. Lookup q20_qty_intermediate[(ps_partkey, ps_suppkey)] → qty_sum. Filter ps_availqty > 0.5 * qty_sum. Collect qualifying (s_name, s_address).
consumer_branches.notes: ~0.7% part filter × 4% nation ≈ ~2.2K qualifying rows before availqty check.

stages.notes: Parallelize with OpenMP across row chunks. Each thread maintains thread-local accumulators. Merge after the loop. HDD sequential read at ~150MB/s → ~2s I/O for 320MB. ps_comment column is NOT read (excluded from output schema), saving ~150MB I/O.

stages.description: Handle queries that do not participate in any shared fused scan. Q22 scans customer independently with index-based NOT EXISTS check.

operations.action: Scan customer: filter c_phone SUBSTRING(1,2) IN ('13','31','23','29','30','18','17'). Compute global avg(c_acctbal) for qualifying customers with acctbal > 0. Filter c_acctbal > avg. Check NOT EXISTS via custkey_to_orders grouped_fk index (if offset[custkey+1]-offset[custkey] == 0 → no orders). Accumulate count and sum(c_acctbal) by country code.
operations.notes: Two-pass: first pass computes avg(c_acctbal), second pass filters and checks NOT EXISTS. ~28% phone filter × ~acctbal filter × NOT EXISTS. 7 output groups. Customer is 120MB, fits in memory.

stages.description: Per-query finalization: compute derived values, sort, apply limits, format, write CSV. Each query finalizes independently. Can be parallelized across queries using thread pool.

operations.action: compute AVG from SUM/COUNT for qty, price, discount. Sort by (returnflag ASC, linestatus ASC). Output CSV. 4 rows.
filter to rows where ps_supplycost = min per partkey. Sort by (s_acctbal DESC, n_name ASC, s_name ASC, p_partkey ASC). Limit 100. Output CSV.
extract top-10 from heap. Sort by (revenue DESC, o_orderdate ASC). Output CSV.
sort by (o_orderpriority ASC). Output CSV. 5 rows.
sort by (revenue DESC). Output CSV. 5 rows.
output single scalar. Output CSV. 1 row.
sort by (supp_nation ASC, cust_nation ASC, l_year ASC). Output CSV. 4 rows.
compute ratio = brazil_volume / total_volume per year. Sort by (o_year ASC). Output CSV. 2 rows.
sort by (nation ASC, o_year DESC). Output CSV. ~175 rows.
extract top-20 from heap by revenue DESC. Output CSV.
compute threshold = total_value * 0.0001. Filter partkeys where value > threshold. Sort by (value DESC). Output CSV.
sort by (l_shipmode ASC). Output CSV. 2 rows.
scan count_per_customer array (including 0-count customers): build histogram c_count → custdist. Sort by (custdist DESC, c_count DESC). Output CSV. ~40 rows.
compute 100.0 * promo_revenue / total_revenue. Output CSV. 1 row.
scan supplier_revenue array, find max revenue. Probe supplier_pk_idx for supplier details. Sort by (s_suppkey ASC). Output CSV.
extract distinct supplier counts per (brand, type, size) group. Sort by (supplier_cnt DESC, p_brand ASC, p_type ASC, p_size ASC). Output CSV.
for each qualifying partkey, compute avg_qty = sum_qty/count. Sum l_extendedprice for rows where l_quantity < 0.2 * avg_qty. Output sum/7.0. Output CSV. 1 row.

scan orderkey_qty_sum array, collect orderkeys where sum > 300. Probe orders_pk_idx for o_orderdate, o_totalprice, o_custkey. Probe customer_pk_idx for c_name. Sort by (o_totalprice DESC, o_orderdate ASC). Limit 100. Output CSV.
output single scalar. Output CSV. 1 row.
sort collected (s_name, s_address) by s_name ASC. Output CSV.
resolve per-orderkey EXISTS/NOT EXISTS logic from accumulated multi-supplier tracking. Count by s_name. Sort by (numwait DESC, s_name ASC). Limit 100. Output CSV.
sort by (cntrycode ASC). Output CSV. 7 rows.

parallelism_opportunities.notes: fused_scan_orders and independent_queries have no data dependencies on fused_scan_lineitem and can run concurrently with it if I/O bandwidth allows. On HDD, concurrent random I/O may cause seek thrashing; on SSD this would be beneficial. Recommend sequential on HDD.

estimated_io_summary.savings_vs_independent: Each of the 22 queries scanning independently would read ~25GB total. Fused execution reads ~6.1GB — a 4x I/O reduction.
